title: Art Nouveau & the Decorative Arts
description: Sinuous line, gilded ornament, and the whiplash curve across print, glass, and design.

items.title: The Tree of Life (Stoclet Frieze)
items.description_narrative: Gustav Klimt's 'The Tree of Life' is an opulent design, featuring a spiraling tree with symbolic motifs and stylized figures, embodying themes of life, death, and spiritual transcendence. This work is a renowned part of the Stoclet Frieze, a monumental decorative commission in the Art Nouveau style.
items.tags: gustav klimt, art nouveau, symbolism, tree of life, decorative arts, frieze, austrian art, spiritual

items.title: Pallas Athene
items.description_narrative: Gustav Klimt's "Pallas Athene" depicts the Greek goddess in a formidable stance, adorned with symbolic armor and an intense gaze. The artwork exemplifies Klimt's distinctive style, combining detailed realism with decorative flatness and symbolic ornamentation.
items.tags: goddess, symbolism, art nouveau, vienna secession, allegorical, female figure, decorative

items.title: Danaë
items.description_narrative: Gustav Klimt's "Danaë" depicts the mythological princess enveloped in a shower of golden rain, symbolizing Zeus's divine impregnation. The artwork showcases Klimt's distinct use of opulent gold and decorative motifs, emphasizing the figure's sensuality and the theme of awakening.
items.tags: danaë, mythology, symbolism, sensuality, art nouveau, golden phase, erotic, decorative

items.title: The Beethoven Frieze
items.description_narrative: The Beethoven Frieze, a monumental wall painting by Gustav Klimt, vividly interprets Richard Wagner's commentary on Beethoven's Ninth Symphony. This powerful work traces humanity's journey through suffering and hostile forces towards a radiant vision of joy and artistic fulfillment.
items.tags: vienna secession, symbolism, art nouveau, mural, allegory, music, human struggle, monumental

items.title: The Slav Epic: The Apotheosis of the Slavs
items.description_narrative: This monumental work, 'The Apotheosis of the Slavs,' forms a pivotal part of Alphonse Mucha's ambitious 'The Slav Epic' series. It symbolically encapsulates the entire history and destiny of the Slavic peoples, expressing a profound sense of national pride and unity.
items.tags: slavic history, monumental painting, allegory, symbolism, nationalism, czech art

items.title: Strawberry Thief
items.description_narrative: William Morris's "Strawberry Thief" is an iconic textile design showcasing a repeating pattern of thrushes attempting to steal strawberries amidst an abundance of flowers and foliage. This intricate and vibrant design exemplifies Morris's deep appreciation for nature and his commitment to handcrafted beauty.
items.tags: textile design, arts and crafts, natural motifs, birds, patterns, decorative art

items.title: Trellis
items.cultural_context: Arts and Crafts Movement, British, 19th century
items.description_narrative: William Morris's 'Trellis' is an early and iconic wallpaper design featuring intricate birds and winding branches set against a repeating lattice pattern. This work exemplifies Morris's commitment to natural forms and meticulous craftsmanship within the decorative arts.
items.tags: wallpaper, arts and crafts, pattern, nature, birds, lattice, decorative, design

items.title: Acanthus
items.description_narrative: This artwork by William Morris showcases his signature style, often featuring intricate, stylized botanical patterns derived from nature. It exemplifies the Arts and Crafts Movement's emphasis on handcrafted beauty and the integration of art into everyday life.
items.tags: arts and crafts, botanical, pattern, decorative arts, victorian, british, nature

items.title: Magnolia and Irises
items.description_narrative: This artwork from Tiffany Studios showcases their renowned craftsmanship and distinctive style. It captures the delicate beauty of magnolias and irises, a common motif in their decorative works.
items.tags: floral, nature, art nouveau, american art, decorative arts, craftsmanship, irises, magnolias

items.title: The Peacock Skirt
items.description_narrative: Aubrey Beardsley's striking illustration, "The Peacock Skirt," depicts a richly stylized figure adorned in a gown inspired by peacock feathers. This iconic black-and-white artwork is renowned for its intricate lines, decorative quality, and its association with Oscar Wilde's play Salomé.
items.tags: art nouveau, aestheticism, illustration, salomé, decorative, black and white, symbolism, elegant

items.title: The Dancer's Reward
items.description_narrative: This striking illustration depicts Salome holding the severed head of John the Baptist, a key image from Aubrey Beardsley's work for Oscar Wilde's play 'Salomé'. Rendered in his distinctive high-contrast black-and-white style, it exemplifies Beardsley's characteristic blend of the macabre and the beautiful.
items.tags: art nouveau, symbolism, decadent, illustration, grotesque, macabre, biblical, salome

items.title: Neptune's Horses
items.description_narrative: Walter Crane's iconic painting depicts a dynamic procession of powerful horses, guided by the sea god Neptune, emerging from the churning waves. This work evokes a sense of mythic grandeur and the untamed force of nature.
items.tags: mythology, symbolism, arts and crafts, pre-raphaelite, english art, painting, epic

items.title: Ver Sacrum
items.description_narrative: Koloman Moser was a leading figure in the Vienna Secession and frequently contributed to its official journal, Ver Sacrum. His graphic designs and illustrations for the magazine are iconic examples of the bold, decorative style of Austrian Art Nouveau.
items.tags: vienna secession, art nouveau, graphic design, illustration, fin de siècle, austrian art, symbolism
